drg.description: Simple Pneumonia and Pleurisy with CC

timeline.text: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 48-year-old male admitted for community-acquired pneumonia. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.73, creatinine 0.97-1.01, hemoglobin 13.3-13.5, platelets 289-296, sodium 125-128, wbc 8.9-9.4; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 81-85, map 89-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 117-122, spo2 95-96, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Chest x-ray: right lower lobe opacity; Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day; Sodium chloride 1 g PO TID
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.96-1, hemoglobin 13.3-13.4, platelets 292-296, sodium 128-131, wbc 8.9-9.6; vitals dbp 75-77, heart_rate 79-84, map 89-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 117-123, spo2 96-97, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia ruled out. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 48-year-old male, length of stay 5 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Community-acquired pneumonia. Hypertension. Hyponatremia ruled out. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
